title: Bolt User App (utilities/<id>.yaml) v1
description: The one schema for a Bolt User App file: utilities/<id>.yaml in an app folder, a User Apps folder or a .boltpack. It is documentation, not an enforcement boundary: Bolt itself refuses a file that breaks a rule, and Bolt also checks things a schema cannot say (a command is split into arguments and run without a shell, a {{variable}} is never inside quotes, a recognize regex must compile). Unknown fields are refused, and so are the company-admin connector fields. The limits below (kinds, view and action limits, patterns) are mirrored from schema/bolt-rules.json in the bolt-apps repository, and a test keeps them equal. The gallery accepts runtime: transform only; personal apps may use bridge and http_local. Guide: https://sparcle.app/docs/extend/agent-guide/ Bolt also checks what a schema cannot say: duplicate action ids, at most one primary action, that view_arg names a declared arg, and the rules about commands and placeholders.

schema_version.description: 1 or 2. 2 makes right_widget bind problems errors for an app file; a pack is checked strictly either way. (The listing bolt-app.json has its own schema_version, always 1.)

runtime.description: transform: reshape text, no command and no network. http_local: one GET or POST to a service on this computer. bridge: run one program and turn its output into rows.

emits.description: File makes a row with an absolute path act as a file. Use Generic when unsure.

from.description: Only query.word(N) exists: the Nth word typed after the key, counting from 0.

actions.description: Buttons on a row and in the pane footer. Bolt shows at most 6 footer buttons in all (these first, then the row's own, trimmed to fit); the authoring kit keeps to 3. Bolt also refuses duplicate action ids and more than one primary.

args.description: Each key must be the name of an entry in the top-level args.

binary.description: A program name looked up on PATH, never a path.

flags.description: Any of i, m, s, u. g and y are refused.

template.description: {value} is replaced with the current text.

from.description: A regular expression. Nested unbounded repeats such as (a+)+ are refused.

host.description: Loopback only. Defaults to 127.0.0.1. Ports 13017-13027 and 15432-15441 belong to Bolt and are refused.

path.description: Starts with / and must not start with // (a protocol-relative address), must not contain a backslash or a control character. {{var}} values are percent-encoded. Bolt must parse the final URL and require the hostname and the port to equal the configured loopback host and port, and must check every redirect target against the same loopback origin.

rows_path.description: Dotted path to the array of rows inside a JSON reply, such as models or result.items.

additionalProperties.description: A literal with no ${ in it, or exactly one ${env:NAME} where NAME is on the allowed list (the same list as bridge.env_passthrough). Any other placeholder is refused.

env.description: Each key is a variable the app may read (the env_passthrough list) and its value is exactly that variable: "NAME": "${env:NAME}". A gallery app cannot forward a variable under another name. Mirrors env_destination_refusal in the launcher.

env_passthrough.description: Environment variables the command reads. Commands start with an empty environment plus a fixed set Bolt chooses; an app may add only these names (hosts, regions, profiles, config paths, public identifiers). Credentials, loader and interpreter settings, proxies and Bolt settings are never forwarded to a gallery app. The list is the same in the launcher and in schema/bolt-rules.json (env.benign_passthrough); keep them in step.

cwd.description: Absent: a fresh private folder for each run.

permissions.description: Optional declared permissions. Today they are shown at install and checked against what the app files use; they are NOT enforced at run time, and a personal script (tier 3) runs as you.

network.description: Sites the app code talks to. Declared and shown, not checked against the script.

links.description: Sites a url action may open.

allOf.description: view_arg must name an arg bound with from: query.word(N) (the name match is checked by Bolt).

argvString.description: One program and its arguments. No ; && || | backtick or $( outside a {{variable}}. A {{variable}} is written bare, never inside quotes. No ~ expansion: use {{home}}.

kind.description: run: one click runs THIS app once with the fixed query_template (the same consent and run log as pressing Enter).

label.description: Bolt keeps 40 characters of a label and the footer button shows the first 14. A label that is one of Allow, Approve, Delete, Confirm, Cancel, Deny, OK, Yes, No, Remove, Unlock or Sign in is shown as "App: <word>" (so a button cannot pass for a Bolt prompt); the toolkit warns about it (action_label_reserved).

target.description: row, or list (a utility action with target: list routes every row).

url_template.description: A web address template. It must be either a literal http:// or https:// address, or a single {{row.field}} placeholder. No other scheme can be written here: javascript:, data:, file: and vbscript: are refused, and control characters are refused. Bolt must still parse the rendered URL and refuse any scheme other than http or https.

primary.description: At most one action may be primary. A run action is never primary.

icon.description: Optional footer-button icon; a name outside this list is refused. Case matters.

query_template.description: Fixed text: a run action runs this app once with it, so no {{ placeholder.

actionIds.description: Ids of entries in the top-level actions.

widget.description: How the result list on the left looks.

title_field.description: Row field shown as the title. parse: lines rows have line and idx.

searchable.description: Accepted and does nothing. Once the app has rows Bolt filters them as you type (title and subtitle); an app with dispatch.choices shows its confirm choices instead.

view_arg.description: Name of the declared arg (from query.word(N)) whose value selects a view. Required when views is present, and refused without views.

views.description: At most 8 views, including the overview. A run whose view_arg value matches a key draws that view's right pane; any other run uses the top-level right_widget.

kind.description: Which pane the launcher draws on the right. Personal apps must not use image, color, weather, date or calc (Bolt shows "cannot show app data"); map reads the launcher's own state and takes no bind keys. Chart types are line, bar and sparkline. Source: the launcher ALLOWED_RIGHT_WIDGET_KIND and the launcher.

oneOf.description: A single card from bind: title, subtitle, actions.

The launcher's own map state: it reads nothing from bind, so any bind key is refused (an error from schema_version 2). It cannot show your rows. For a place, add a url action that opens it in Maps (Open in Maps link).

Bolt shows "This app asks for an image pane, which cannot show app data. Use image_grid for pictures." instead of your rows. The pane reads its own state and ignores bind. A personal app must not use it.

Bolt shows "This app asks for a calc pane, which cannot show app data. Use table, detail, cards or chart." instead of your rows. The pane reads its own state and ignores bind. A personal app must not use it.

Bolt shows "This app asks for a color pane, which cannot show app data. Use table, detail, cards or chart." instead of your rows. The pane reads its own state and ignores bind. A personal app must not use it.

Bolt shows "This app asks for a weather pane, which cannot show app data. Use table, detail, cards or chart." instead of your rows. The pane reads its own state and ignores bind. A personal app must not use it.

Bolt shows "This app asks for a date pane, which cannot show app data. Use table, detail, cards or chart." instead of your rows. The pane reads its own state and ignores bind. A personal app must not use it.
Markdown body from bind: title, subtitle, body, actions.
Rich detail card: media, title, subtitle, label and value facts, optional body and tiles_above.

A chart of the rows. bind.type is line, bar, sparkline, pie, donut or area; pie, donut, area and bind.series need Bolt 0.1.182 or newer (a 181 refuses the whole pack). Any other value is refused (an error from schema_version 2).
A table of the rows, with columns, sort and totals.
Cards or tiles from the rows (layout grid or tiles).
A label and value detail of the selected row.
A collapsible JSON tree from bind.source.
A text diff from bind.left and bind.right.
A grid of pictures from bind.src (1 to 8 columns).
A grid, matrix or calendar of numbers shaded in five steps (Bolt 0.1.182 and later; a Bolt 0.1.181 refuses the whole pack that uses it).
One value on a min to max scale as a ring or half ring (Bolt 0.1.182 and later; a Bolt 0.1.181 refuses the whole pack that uses it).

mode.description: selected_row: the highlighted row. list_data: all rows.

bind.description: Keys the chosen pane reads; each kind has its own bind schema below. map, image, calc, color, weather and date read nothing.

tiles_above.description: One tile for the selected row, drawn above the facts. Same keys as the cards tiles layout.

hero.description: A full-pane-width picture above the tile and title (Bolt 182 and later; a Bolt 0.1.181 refuses the whole pack that uses it). src is a template that must resolve to an inline data:image URI (png, jpeg, gif, webp, avif or bmp, at most 1 MiB); a web address is never loaded. src may join at most 16 {{ }} references, for example {{row.img1}}{{row.img2}}. A missing or invalid src draws no hero. image_url stays the small avatar.

series.description: Several lines on one chart (type line or area). Bolt 0.1.182 and later; a 181 refuses the whole pack. A series takes values or y and an optional label; a color is refused.

limit.description: A dashed horizontal line at this value. A number or a {{row.x}} reference read from the selected row. Not a number: no line. Bolt 0.1.184 and later; an older Bolt refuses the whole pack (a personal schema_version 1 file loads with a warning and the key does nothing). Set min_bolt_version 0.1.184 in bolt-app.json.

limit_label.description: Words on the limit line, shown clipped to 24 characters. Bolt 0.1.184 and later.

marker.description: Labelled vertical marks, one per row whose field cell is set (not empty, 0, false or null), at most 8, row data only (not with values). label names the field that gives the text, else the cell itself. Bolt 0.1.184 and later.

bars.description: An inline bar under the cell, scaled to the largest shown value of the column. Numeric columns only; zero, negative and non-numbers draw no bar. Bolt 0.1.184 and later.

mark.description: A glyph before the cell text, read from the cell as a tone word (ok, warn, error and so on), by shape not colour. Bolt 0.1.184 and later.

layout.description: tiles needs value. Builds older than 2026-11-07 with the Rich widgets switch off draw the grid instead.

max.description: Draws a meter (gauge) from value to max.
